newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE ON COURSE FOR 2ND STAGE EMU - MERRILL LYNCH.
newsitem.headline: GREECE ON COURSE FOR 2ND STAGE EMU - MERRILL LYNCH.

text.p: Greece has good prospects for participation in the second phase of EMU early in the next century under the leadership of Prime Minister Costas Simitis and his commitment to EU convergence, said Merrill Lynch.

"Simitis' commitment to EU convergence should provide Greece with a good chance to participate in the second phase of EMU early next century," said Merrill Lynch in its April report on Greece's economic and investment outlook.

Further progress will be made on cutting inflation and interest rates this year as the central bank's open market operations and continued use of the hard drachma policy bode well for a tight rein on the CPI.
But the government's year-end inflation target of 4.5 percent will be overshot as price inflation is seen dropping to 5.3 percent by year-end, the report said.
April CPI is expected to ease below 6.0 percent year-on-year. The official figure will be announced by Greece's National Statistics Service (NSS) on Thursday.

"It is easy to sound pessimistic when assessing the likelihood of Greece meeting this year's economic targets. However, this is more a reflection of the severity of the targets rather than doubts in the government's ability to introduce economic reform," the report said.

Greece is relying on strong growth to reduce its budget and public debt burdens as a percent of GDP. It should experience growth above the EU average again this year -- real GDP is seen growing at 2.8 percent with public investment underpinning the expansion.

Although progress has been achieved in reducing the budget deficit in recent years, this year's tough budget target was unlikely to be met. The budget deficit is seen dropping to 5.5 percent of GDP versus the government's 4.2 percent target, Merrill Lynch said.

"The reduction of debt servicing costs remains a key policy for reducing the fiscal deficit over the longer term. Greek public debt is almost twice the 60 percent convergence target. However, provided public debt continues to fall, it should not pose a barrier to EMU entry," said analyst David Calver who authored the report.
The hard-drachma policy -- the backbone of Greece's anti-inflation policy in recent years -- allows for a limited slide versus the ecu, less than suggested by the Greek-EU inflation differential.
"Although no target has been announced for 1997, we continue to expect around a 1.0 percent depreciation of the drachma against the ecu this year," the report said.
The drachma was expected to enter ERM in 1999 and trade comfortably within the ERM normal bands.
Concerns over the adverse effects of the hard drachma on the current account deficit have led to suggestions that the currency may suffer a devaluation prior to ERM entry.
"We believe a one-time devaluation of the drachma is unlikely. An abrupt devaluation could cause a resurgence in inflation and damage the government's credibility in Europe," the report said.
